{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Vendor's Master Services Agreement — 18 findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the MSA against our playbook. Eight positions are compliant as drafted and need no redline — limitation of liability (§ 21), assignment and change of control (§ 24), licence grant (§ 13), audit rights (§ 22), auto-renewal (§ 8.2–8.3), performance warranty (§ 19), Vendor insurance (§ 18) and the absence of any liquidated damages payable by us.

Ten items require change. Three are critical:

- **No indemnity at all.** The outline jumps from Section 19 (Warranties) to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability), yet §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 all assume indemnities exist and § 9.3 cross-references a non-existent Section 20.5. We have inserted a new Section 20 (Vendor IP, breach-of-law, data-incident and wilful-misconduct indemnity; narrow reciprocal Customer indemnity; notice/control/cooperation; procure-modify-replace-refund remedies), which also repairs the broken § 9.3 cross-reference. Note that the § 21.3 Excluded Claims carve-out for "indemnification obligations" only has effect once this insert is accepted.
- **Deliverable ownership reversed (§ 14.2).** Vendor owns every Deliverable we pay for and we receive only a revocable, non-transferable term licence, so we lose access on expiry. We have flipped ownership to Customer with assignment (perpetual, irrevocable, transferable licence as fallback); Vendor still retains Vendor Technology under § 14.3.
- **No termination for convenience.** Section 9 offers only breach, insolvency and performance-failure exits (numbering skips 9.4), and § 2.1 expressly denies termination rights across a three-year term. We have inserted a new § 9.4: 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no early-termination charge.

The commercial lock-in provisions cluster together and are mutually reinforcing: the USD 2,000,000 per year three-year take-or-pay (§ 2.1), the disclose-and-match right of first refusal / MFN (§ 7.2) and the worldwide 24-month non-compete and one-way no-hire (§ 12.4). Each contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity, minimum-volume or most-favoured-customer commitment. Finally, § 28.1 (Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction) is outside our accepted list and conflicts on its face with § 28.2 (exclusive New York County venue); we have moved governing law to New York and left §§ 28.2–28.3 intact. We have also inserted transition assistance and data return obligations at § 10.3, which the drafted exit machinery assumes but nowhere provides.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | Anchored at § 19.5; new Section 20 inserted; § 9.3 cross-reference repaired | Insert Vendor indemnity, narrow Customer indemnity, procedure and remedies |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 | Flip Deliverable ownership to Customer with assignment; delete revocable term licence |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 (with §§ 1.5, 21.3) | No redline; carve-out for indemnification takes effect only once Section 20 is added |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with §§ 24.2–24.4, 13.3) | No redline |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Delete the disclose-and-match precondition to engaging another provider |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 1.5 (with §§ 7.3, 27.3) | No redline; our § 9.4 insert states no early-termination charge applies |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with §§ 13.2–13.3) | No redline; § 14.2 addressed under IP |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 | Delete the 24-month worldwide non-compete |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | Anchored at § 9.3; new § 9.4 inserted | Customer-only convenience right on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 (with Section 23) | No redline |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 28.1 | Replace Singapore law/venue with New York law, aligning with § 28.2 |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Delete the MFN running against us; rely on § 12.3 |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 | Replace three-year take-or-pay with single-year, reducible commitment plus true-up |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 | Narrow to mutual, 12-month, involved-personnel restriction; advertising carve-out; no no-hire |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8.2 (with § 8.3) | No redline |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | Missing | Anchored at § 10.1 (see § 16.5); new § 10.3 inserted | Six months' assistance at then-current rates; machine-readable data return in 30 days; certified deletion |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 (with §§ 19.4–19.5) | No redline |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 | No redline |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following are identified in our playbook as walk-away positions and must be resolved before signature:

1. **§ 2.1 — Three-year, USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights.** Our fallback: no standing commitment; any Order Form commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, ending on termination, with shortfalls handled by carry-forward true-up rather than penalty.
2. **§ 2.1 read with Section 9 — No termination right for Customer.** A three-year term with no convenience exit is unacceptable; our § 9.4 insert (30 days' notice, pro-rata refund, no early-termination charge, no Vendor convenience exit) resolves it.
3. **§ 7.2 — Disclose-and-match right of first refusal.** Operates as de facto exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit. Deletion requested.
4. **§ 12.4 — Worldwide, undefined-scope 24-month post-term non-compete on Customer.** Deletion requested; if Vendor needs protection, we could consider a term-only restriction on one named competing product with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
5. **§ 12.4 — One-way 24-month no-hire covering all Vendor employees, including self-initiated applicants.** Narrowing to the mutual 12-month formulation above is the minimum acceptable outcome.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Send the redline** covering the three critical items first — new Section 20 (indemnity, with the § 9.3 cross-reference repair), § 14.2 Deliverable ownership, and new § 9.4 termination for convenience.
2. **Group the lock-in provisions** (§ 2.1, § 7.2, § 12.4) into a single commercial conversation and anchor it on § 12.3, where Vendor already acknowledges we have made no exclusivity, minimum-volume or most-favoured-customer commitment. Flag the internal inconsistency rather than arguing the point in the abstract.
3. **Raise the drafting defects** with Vendor's counsel: the missing Section 20, the § 9.3 reference to a non-existent Section 20.5, the skipped § 9.4, the § 16.5 reference to an absent Section 11, and the § 28.1/§ 28.2 conflict. These are best framed as clean-up and should move quickly.
4. **Confirm the governing law swap** to New York, leaving §§ 28.2 and 28.3 unchanged so venue and escalation are undisturbed.
5. **Confirm the § 10.3 exit package** with our technical and data teams — six months' assistance, machine-readable export within 30 days and certified deletion — given the hosted health data at issue.
6. **Hold the compliant sections closed.** We should not reopen §§ 8, 13, 18, 19, 21, 22 or 24, and should resist any Vendor attempt to trade them against the items above; the § 21.3 indemnification carve-out in particular depends on our Section 20 insert surviving.
"}
